column2: Taralaka with milk, cotton fruit and leaves; the new flower-tips of apamarga with buffalo-milk —
for a son, with the six half-vegetables; four combinations are declared. Sugar, utpala, flower, akshas, lodhra, sandal and sariva
should be given with rice-water when a woman's pregnancy is leaking; or one should lick parched rice, licorice, sugar, grapes, honey and ghee.
Atarushaka, langali, kakamachi, shipha separately — having smeared below the navel, a woman delivers easily.
Red and white hibiscus flower one should drink in red and white discharge; kesara, brihati root, gopi, yashti, grass and utpala,
with goat's milk and oil — eating it makes hair grow. When hair is falling, this is the stabilizer:

oil of a prastha of amalaka and bhringaraja juice, and an adhaka of milk. "Om homage to the Lord Tryambaka: calm calm, chulu chulu, mili mili, bhinda, Gomanini, Chakrini hum phat — in this village protect the cow-herd, make peace; Ghantakarna, Mahasena, the hero, is said to be of great strength,
the destroyer of epidemics; may that Lord of the world protect me." One should place these two verses separately as the two cow-protecting mantras.
Tara, Mesha, Visha, Danti, Nara, Dirgha, Vana, Rasa: "To the angry Ulka, Mahaulka, Viraulka" is the crest;
to Hyulka, to Rahasaulka — the eight-syllable Vaishnava mantra. On the finger-joints of those bitten, beginning with the little finger,
with the tip of the elder in order one should place the eight-syllable on the head so many times. With the forefinger touching the thumb and the middle finger,
on the palm and thumb, then the transposed and seed-transposed. Red, white, smoky, green, golden, white — three white:
thus these colors, understood by feeling, one should place in order: on heart, mouth, eyes, head, feet, palate, private part, hands and the rest.
One should place also the limbs and seeds; then having placed on hands and body: as in oneself so in the god the placing should be done, without the hand.

One should worship the letters standing in the heart and other places with scents and flowers. Dharma and the rest, Agni and the rest, adharma and the rest one should place in the body, on the seat, on the lotus;
where the filaments, the stamens, the pervading sun, moon and fire — those three circles by their divisions one should place there in order.
Qualities such as tantra, sattva and the rest, and the powers abiding in the filaments: Vimala, Utkarshani, Jnana, Kriya, and Yoga in order;
Prahvi, Satya, Ishana, Anugraha in the middle — having worshipped the yoga-seat, having invoked, one should worship Hari.
Water for the feet, arghya and rinsing, yellow garment and adornment — these five services are all given with the root mantra.
Vasudeva and the rest, four forms in the directions, are to be worshipped; in the corners one should worship Shri, Sarasvati, Rati and Shanti;
conch, discus, mace, lotus, pestle, sword and Sarnga bow, with forest-garland, in the directions and corners one should worship in order.

Having worshipped outside, Tarkshya should be worshipped before the god; Vishvaksena and Someshvara in the middle outside the enclosure. Having honored with the attendants of Indra and the rest, one obtains everything.
With the root, image, limb and knowledge mantras, having done the throwing of rice and the rest, the cooked offering — the milk — one should divide again in three;
having offered one, having offered another, the teacher with disciple should partake of the other; having rinsed and consecrated, the teacher should give to the disciple.
A tooth-stick recited over with the heart, from milk-tree and the like; having cleaned the teeth, having thrown it away, having washed, one should cast it on the ground;
by the east, it goes to the northern or the water-lord's direction — good for one of good mind. Again that disciple coming, protected by a child-binding and the like,
having made on the altar, the wise should sleep with him on a darbha spread. Seeing him well asleep, the disciple at dawn should tell the teacher;
by auspicious signs of success, devotion; with them again the worship of the mandala. One should worship the mandala told as the Bhadra and the rest, giver of all success.
Having bathed and rinsed, having smeared the body with clay with mantras, it is arranged; a man should bathe at a Shiva-tirtha beginning with the Aghamarshana;
having done the hand-consecration, the wise should proceed to worship and the rest. With the root mantra one should make the lotus seat; with it inhalations and retentions;
having joined the self upward at twelve fingers beyond the crest, having dried and burned one's own body, one should flood it with nectar;
having inflated the divine body, one should again lead the self into it. Having done thus there is self-purification; having placed, one should begin the worship.
In order black, white, dark, red, yellow are the mountains and the rest; the mantra letters, Dandin and limbs, in them all the forms;
from thumb to little finger having placed the limbs all round, one should place the mantra-syllable on feet, private part, heart, mouth and head;
having placed the pervading from head onward, one should place the root and limbs. Red, yellow, dark and white seat-feet born of their own times;
one should place one's own limbs with mantras, the bodily parts, adharma and the rest in directions. There the lotus, and the triad of qualities in the solar and other circles;
on the east petal and so on the ninefold beginning with Kama on the pericarp: Vama, Jyeshtha, in order Raudri, Kali, Kalavikarini,
Balavikarini and then Balapramathani, Sarvabhutadamani and the ninth Manonmani;
white, red, pale, yellow, dark, fire-colored and black-red — those powers in the form of flames one should remember in order.
To the endless yoga-seat — having invoked from the heart-lotus Shiva crystal-bright, four-armed, bearing fruit and trident,
with fearlessness and boon, five-faced and three-eyed. On the petals five forms are to be established: Tatpurusha and the rest:
in the east Tatpurusha, white; Aghora eight-armed, black; four-armed and four-faced, yellow, Sadyojata in the west;
Vamadeva amorous, four-faced and four-armed, red; in the north five-faced, in the northeast Ishana, giver of all, white.
One should worship the desired limbs as is fit, the Infinite, the Subtle; Siddheshvara with one eye in the east and other directions;
Ekarudra, Trinetra, Shrikantha, Shikhandin in the northeast and other corners — these Vidyeshas lotus-seated;
white, yellow, pale, red, smoky, red, ruddy and black, with trident, thunderbolt, arrow, breath and arms, four-faced;
Uma, Chandesha, Nandisha, Mahakala, Ganeshvara, Bull, Bhringi, Riti, Skanda — in the north and so on one should worship;
vajra, shakti and staff, sword, noose, banner, mace, trident, discus and lotus one should worship; in the east and so on having worshipped the god.
Then the disciple, made fit, should be made to drink the five cow-products. Having rinsed, sprinkled with the eye-endings, one should bind the eyes with the eye-mantra;
one should lead the disciple through the door to the south of the pavilion; seated on a kusha seat and the like there the teacher should purify him;
having withdrawn the primary principles, dissolution in the supreme reality in order; again the teacher should produce the disciple by the creation path;
having then placed on the disciple, one should lead him round clockwise; having brought to the west door, one should have a handful of flowers thrown;
on whomever the flowers fall, that one's name and so on should be declared. At the side in the sacrifice ground in a dug pit, with girdle,
having produced the Shiva-fire and worshipped, again with the disciple one should worship; having withdrawn the disciple, in the likeness of oneself by meditation, dissolution in order;
having produced again, one should place consecrated darbha in his hand; one should offer the principles beginning with earth with the heart-mantra and the rest;
having offered a hundred for each, one should offer with the sky root mantra; having offered, one should make the full oblation; with the weapon eight oblations;
expiation for purification; then one should complete the rest. Having worshipped the pot consecrated with mantras, one should consecrate the child on the seat;
having given the covenant to the disciple, one should worship one's teacher with gold and the like. Initiation into the five-syllable is told; likewise for Vishnu and the rest.
On the bank at Kashi the Great Yoga; at Viraja the conqueror of enemies; at Vishakhayupa the Unconquered; in Nepal the Sustainer of the worlds;
at Dvaraka know Krishna; at Mandara Madhusudana; at Lokakula the destroyer of enemies; at Shalagrama one should remember Hari;
Purusha at Purushavata and at Vimala the Lord of the world; Ananta in the Saindhava forest; the Sarnga-bearer in Dandaka;
Shauri at Utpalavartaka; the Lord of Shri at Narmada; Damodara at Raivataka; the Water-Sleeper at Nanda;
Gopishvara at the Sindhu ocean; Achyuta at Mahendra, they know; at Sahyadri the god of gods; Vaikuntha in the Magadha forest;
the destroyer of all sin in Vindhya; Purushottama in Odra; know the Self in the heart, giver of enjoyment and liberation to reciters.
Vaishravana in tree after tree; Shiva at crossing after crossing; Rama on mountain after mountain; Madhusudana everywhere;
Nara on earth, and in the sky; Garudadhvaja at Vashishtha; remembering Vasudeva everywhere one shares enjoyment and liberation.
Having recited these names of Vishnu one obtains everything. In these holy places whatever ancestral rite, gift, recitation and libation
is all increased a crore-fold; dying he becomes Brahman-formed. One who reads or hears this becomes stainless and attains heaven.

Om homage to the Lord Unmatta-Rudra: bhrama bhrama, bhramaya bhramaya, terrify so-and-so, bewilder bewilder, in the terrible form, hum phat tha tha. Recited at night in a cremation ground, one should offer three lakh with honey; on the funeral fire with rogues' fuel the enemy is made to wander constantly.
A black image made with golden ochre, with golden needles, having recited, one should pierce it at the throat or heart; the enemy dies.
Ash from a donkey's tail-hair funeral pyre, brahmadandi and markati: that powder, recited over, thrown in a house or on the head, causes uprooting.

Bhrigu and sky, with blazing fire, Bhrigu and fire and "varma phat" — thus, in the thousand-spoked, "hum phat; to Achakra svaha" the heart; "to Vichakra" Shiva, the crest; "to Chakra" then the armor; "to Vichakra" then the eye;
to Sanchakra the weapon is told; "to Jvalachakra" as before. Sarnga, Sudarshana, remover of minor seizers, accomplishing all;
one should place its letters on head, eyes, mouth, heart, private part and feet. Seated on a discus-lotus, fire-bright, with tusks, four-armed,
holding conch, discus, mace, lotus, rod and goad in hands, with bow, tawny-haired, covering the three worlds —
